title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Delivery of Goods without Original Bill of Lading

articles.content_en: For the purposes of these Provisions, original bills of lading include straight bills of lading, order bills of lading and bearer bills of lading.

Where a carrier, in violation of legal provisions, delivers goods without an original bill of lading, thereby harming the bill of lading rights of the holder of the original bill of lading, the holder of the original bill of lading may request the carrier to bear civil liability for the losses caused thereby.

Where the carrier causes losses to the holder of an original bill of lading by delivering goods without an original bill of lading, the holder of the original bill of lading may request the carrier to bear liability for breach of contract, or to bear tort liability.
Where the holder of an original bill of lading requests the carrier to bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading, the provisions of the Maritime Code shall apply; where the Maritime Code has no provisions, the provisions of other laws shall apply.
Where a carrier bears civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading, the provisions of Article 56 of the Maritime Code concerning limitation of liability shall not apply.

Where a person taking delivery of goods has taken delivery of the goods from the carrier by presenting a forged bill of lading, the consignee holding the original bill of lading may request the carrier to bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading.

The amount of compensation for losses caused to the holder of an original bill of lading by the carrier's delivery of goods without an original bill of lading shall be calculated according to the value of the goods at the time of shipment plus freight and insurance premium.

Where a carrier, in accordance with the law of the place where the discharge port specified in the bill of lading is located, must deliver the goods carried to the port to the local customs or port authorities, it shall not bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading.

Where goods carried to the port are not declared to customs by any person within the time limit prescribed by law, and the customs have taken the goods and disposed of them by sale according to law, or the court has ruled according to law to auction the goods retained by the carrier, and the carrier claims exemption from the liability for delivering the goods, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Where the carrier, upon the request of the shipper under a straight bill of lading, suspends the carriage, returns the goods, changes the place of arrival, or delivers the goods to another consignee, and the consignee holding the straight bill of lading requests the carrier to bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Where a carrier issues several original bills of lading in one set and, after delivering the goods to the person who first presents an original bill of lading, other holders of the same original bills of lading request the carrier to bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading, the People's Court shall not support the request.

The holder of an original bill of lading may request the carrier who delivered goods without an original bill of lading and the person who took delivery of the goods without an original bill of lading to bear joint and several liability for compensation.

Where a shipper who actually delivered the goods to the carrier and holds an order bill of lading, although the shipper's identity is not stated on the original bill of lading, requests the carrier to bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading in accordance with the contract of carriage of goods by sea, the People's Court shall support the claim.

After the carrier has delivered the goods without an original bill of lading, where the holder of the original bill of lading and the person who took delivery of the goods without an original bill of lading have reached an agreement on payment of the price of the goods, the failure to pay the agreed amount shall not affect the right of the holder of the original bill of lading to request the carrier to bear civil liability for delivery of goods without an original bill of lading for the losses suffered.

An action instituted by the holder of an original bill of lading on the ground that the carrier delivered goods without an original bill of lading shall be governed by the provisions of Article 257 of the Maritime Code, and the limitation period shall be one year, calculated from the date on which the carrier should have delivered the goods.
Where the holder of an original bill of lading institutes an action in tort on the ground that the carrier and the person who took delivery of the goods without an original bill of lading jointly committed the act of delivering goods without an original bill of lading, the limitation of action shall be governed by the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article.

For an action instituted by the holder of an original bill of lading on the ground that the carrier delivered goods without an original bill of lading, the interruption of limitation shall be governed by the provisions of Article 267 of the Maritime Code.
Where the holder of an original bill of lading institutes an action in tort on the ground that the carrier and the person who took delivery of the goods without an original bill of lading jointly committed the act of delivering goods without an original bill of lading, the interruption of limitation shall be governed by the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article.
